new_statements.quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as “composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two,” implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. [...] In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. [Table A.2:] Yutanduchi de Guerrero Ytd Yutn mab Alta:E
new_statements.citation: Josserand, Judy Kathryn. 1983. Mixtec Dialect History (Proto-Mixtec and Modern Mixtec Text). PhD diss., Tulane University, p. 180 — as quoted in Carroll, Lucien S. 2015. Ixpantepec Nieves Mixtec Word Prosody. PhD diss., UC San Diego, p. 86.
new_statements.locator: Carroll 2015 sec. 4.2.1 p. 86 (quoting Josserand 1983:180); Table A.2 p. 276
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: lines 5443-5446 (printed p. 86, sec. 4.2.1) read exactly 'Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior.'; line 5490 (still p. 86) has 'In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec.'; line 16819 (Table A.2, printed p. 276) has the row 'Yutanduchi de Guerrero Ytd Yutn mab Alta:E' (the only other Ytd hit, line 17028, is a map label). All three pieces of the reported quote are verbatim at the stated locators (the '[...]' elision spans the intervening survey of Ayut…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of the bimoraic/disyllabic root 'couplet', i.e. the penultimate syllable of canonical disyllabic roots; this is Josserand's family-wide generalization over her 120-town dialect survey, which includes Yutanduchi de Guerrero (code Yutn, Eastern Alta). No Yutanduchi-specific stress description exists.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Yutanduchi; Carroll notes for other varieties that vocalic enclitics may or may not shift stress (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala) and that Atatlahuca polysyllables take penultimate stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the root couplet (stem), not the phonological word with clitics; statement is comparative/family-level, not based on Yutanduchi citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: All evidence refers to the town variety of Yutanduchi de Guerrero (Josserand code Yutn; MixteCoDB yuta11; INALI 'tu'un savi de Yutanduchi de Guerrero'), which is exactly Glottolog yuta1240 / ISO mab (Eastern Alta Mixtec). The stress statement itself is Josserand's pan-Mixtec generalization, not a description of this variety.
